Identify K with binary-sequence space; finite-coordinate cylinders form a clopen basis and coordinatewise multiplication and inversion are continuous. To prove compactness in ZF, suppose an open cover has no finite subcover. Call a finite binary word bad when its cylinder has no finite subcover; the empty word is bad. At least one of the two children of any bad word is bad, since finite covers of both children combine into a finite cover of the parent. Recursively take the least bad child, choosing 0 when both are bad, to obtain a definite infinite path x all of whose prefix cylinders are bad. An open cover member containing x contains some prefix cylinder, a contradiction. Distinct paths are separated by clopen cylinders, so K is Hausdorff. For a continuous ρ:K→GL(V), finite-dimensional coordinate norm equivalence makes ρ operator-norm continuous at e. Choose a product cylinder subgroup N fixing finitely many initial coordinates with ||ρ(g)−I||<1 for every g∈N. Every g∈N has order two. If ρ(g)≠I, choose v with w=(ρ(g)−I)v≠0; then ρ(g)w=−w and ||ρ(g)−I||≥2, contradiction. Thus N⊆kerρ and contains a nonidentity tail element, so ρ is not faithful. Compactness is proved directly by a definable least-child argument on the binary tree; no form of choice or Tychonoff is used.
